projects.title: Phishguard- Phising Website Detector
projects.description:
PhisGuard is a lightweight yet highly effective phishing-detection system designed to keep users safe from malicious links and deceptive websites. At its core, PhisGuard uses a Decision Tree classification model, trained on real-world phishing and legitimate URL datasets to deliver fast and reliable detection.
With an accuracy of around 90%, the system analyzes URL patterns, domain features, and structural attributes to instantly classify whether a link is safe or suspicious. PhisGuard provides clear alerts, seamless integration, and real-time protection — without the heavy computational cost of deep learning models.
Whether you're browsing online, checking emails, or validating shared links, PhisGuard ensures every click is smarter and safer.
PhisGuard — Simple, accurate, and efficient phishing protection powered by Decision Trees.

projects.title: Spam Detection AI
projects.description:
The Spam Email Detector is a machine learning–based text classification system designed to accurately detect spam messages in real time. Built using classical ML algorithms and trained on the combined_data.csv dataset, this system analyzes email or SMS text and instantly classifies it as Spam or Not Spam with high precision.
At the core, the project uses a Decision Tree Classifier,Naïve Bayes and SVM classifiers achieving an impressive 99.06% accuracy during evaluation. Allowing users to switch between models and compare performance in real-time.
By extracting text features using TF-IDF and applying supervised learning techniques, the detector quickly identifies suspicious keywords, patterns, and structures commonly found in phishing or spam messages. The result is an intuitive, visually appealing dashboard that shows:
🔍 Confidence Score
📬 Spam vs. Not Spam Probability
🤖 Model Used (Decision Tree / Naïve Bayes / SVM)
⚡ Real-time text analysis
The detector is optimized for practical use, educational demonstrations, and ML workflow understanding. With its clean UI, interactive model selection, and extremely high accuracy, it serves as a complete end-to-end ML project—from preprocessing to deployment.
Spam Email Detector — Fast, accurate, and model-flexible. Powered by Decision Tree (99.06% accurate).

projects.title: VaquaH-AC Products & Services Web App.
projects.description:
VaquaH Cooling Service A modern web app for discovering AC products and booking cooling services. It includes a product catalog, detailed pages, cart and checkout flow, service appointments, orders, contracts, and a user dashboard.

Highlights Products: Rich catalog with images, specs, and feature highlights Commerce: Cart, checkout, order history and status Services: Appointment booking with confirmation and updates Contracts: Plan selection and contract management Experience: Fast, responsive, mobile‑first UI with accessible components Tech Overview Frontend React (Vite), React Router Tailwind CSS + Shadcn UI TanStack Query for client‑side caching and syncing Context-based state (Auth, Cart) and modular service layer Backend (Briefing, high‑level only) Node.js application that powers product, order, appointment, and contract workflows Layered architecture (routing/controllers → domain services → data access) Pluggable integrations for authentication, payments, and data storage Environment-driven configuration; no secrets stored in the repository Emphasis on input validation, consistent error handling, and observability hooks Project Structure src/components — Reusable UI blocks src/pages — Route-level pages src/context — Providers (Auth, Cart) src/services — Frontend data-access modules src/lib — App configuration and utilities src/utils — Non-UI helpers backend/ — Node.js server (domain services and HTTP handlers) Local Development Install dependencies npm install cd frontend && npm install cd ../backend && npm install Start concurrent dev servers npm run dev Build production assets npm run build Output is generated in frontend/dist.

Acknowledgements Built with React, Tailwind, Shadcn UI, TanStack Query, and a lightweight Node.js service layer.

Within seconds:

Signals start adapting.

This isn’t the future.

Team: 𝟮𝗔𝗠 𝗖𝗢𝗗𝗘𝗥𝗦
Poorvanshi Kochar, Hetav Shah, Leena Shah, Fenil Solanki

Signal Agent → adjusts traffic lights dynamically
Routing Agent → finds safest, smartest diversions
Alert Agent → communicates instantly with the public

All of them working together — in under 3 seconds.

A few days back, I learned something without even participating in a hackathon 😄
There was a Google Developer Groups (GDG) hackathon at our university.
I didn’t take part — no team, tight schedule.
A day before, a classmate asked:
👉 which AI IDE I use
👉 what I use for frontend & backend
⚛️ React
🔥 Firebase
🤖 Antigravity
The next day at 5:30 PM while I was in library(rare 😅), he asked how to deploy.
I explained the Vercel flow.
Around 7 PM, while I was still in the library (very rare 😅), I got a call:
“Vercel isn’t recognizing the repo and we need to submit till 8-9 pm.”
So I walked to the reading area in the opposite building —
and instantly saw the issue 👀
The project was uploaded as a ZIP file 📦
Then I asked:
“Do you have Git installed?”
The answer was:
“I don’t know.”
I installed Git , pushed the repo properly, and deployed — live 🚀
I also guided them on backend deployment using Render for later.
This wasn’t just one team — I helped with the same issue 3–5 teams that evening(all teams present there).
Most were 8–9.5 CGPA rankers.
I’m a 7.15 CGPA struggler 😅
That day made one thing clear:
fundamentals beat last-minute cramming.
Even if the scores are lower.
Even if the journey is slower.
Because when it’s time to build, debug, deploy, and fix things under pressure —
fundamentals show up.
